The evidence suggests that Magnesium Citrate may act as a mediator in the development of this disease by influencing calcium metabolism. Specifically, Magnesium Citrate is linked to Hypercalcemia Disease, which is characterized by elevated calcium levels in the blood, and this condition is further associated with Calcium Gluconate, which in turn is linked to Postmenopausal Osteoporosis. The integration of these pathways implies that Magnesium Citrate may exert a role in modulating calcium homeostasis, potentially through its effects on calcium absorption or excretion, thereby contributing to the development of postmenopausal osteoporosis. The evidence from these paths highlights a potential mechanism by which Magnesium Citrate could influence bone density in postmenopausal women, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
